sentences.text: Sir Stephen Timms has been looking into disability benefits in England and Wales for the past year and found the set up was "no longer fit for purpose".
sentences.article_title: Pip assessments need 'fundamental overhaul', report to say

sentences.text: Writing in the Times , external , he said his review, to be published on Tuesday, would recommend people with the most severe conditions have a "fast track" process which is "less burdensome".
sentences.article_title: Pip assessments need 'fundamental overhaul', report to say

sentences.text: It comes after a separate review into young people not in education, employment or training (Neets) recommended Pip be scrapped and replaced for under-25s.
sentences.article_title: Pip assessments need 'fundamental overhaul', report to say

sentences.text: Sir Stephen, who produced his report alongside disability groups, carers, clinicians and MPs, said that while Pip had the "right aims" when it was created, there have been "marked shifts in the nature of disability and ill health" in the 13 years since.
sentences.article_title: Pip assessments need 'fundamental overhaul', report to say

sentences.text: He said there had been "substantial growth in claims for mental health and neurodiverse conditions as well as changes to wider society and the workplace".
sentences.article_title: Pip assessments need 'fundamental overhaul', report to say

sentences.text: "For those with the most severe conditions and end of life care, the review recommends a fast track which is less burdensome, with assessment capacity freed up for other cases.
sentences.article_title: Pip assessments need 'fundamental overhaul', report to say

sentences.text: "Where claimants do not have additional costs or care needs, we should be signposting them to services and support." He added: "Someone with a lifelong or degenerative illness should not need regular reassessments which feel adversarial and unnecessary.
sentences.article_title: Pip assessments need 'fundamental overhaul', report to say

sentences.text: More than 130 MPs, including 120 from Labour, signed an amendment to reject plans to cut disability and sickness-related benefit payments in 2025.
sentences.article_title: Pip assessments need 'fundamental overhaul', report to say

sentences.text: The rebels said they opposed the plans because of the number of people expected to be pushed into relative poverty and a lack of consultation at the time.
sentences.article_title: Pip assessments need 'fundamental overhaul', report to say

sentences.text: The government welcomed the Milburn review, which included a recommendation to move those aged 18 to 24 off Pip and the health element of universal credit, and onto an entirely new benefits system.
sentences.article_title: Pip assessments need 'fundamental overhaul', report to say

sentences.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he thought the "same philosophy" could be applied "right through the age range".
sentences.article_title: Pip assessments need 'fundamental overhaul', report to say

sentences.text: At this stage it is unclear how both of the reviews will complement one another.
sentences.article_title: Pip assessments need 'fundamental overhaul', report to say

sentences.text: No 10 has said the government would consider the Timms review "alongside Milburn's and respond in the coming weeks".
sentences.article_title: Pip assessments need 'fundamental overhaul', report to say

sentences.text: Downing Street has not ruled out the possibility that some people who currently receive Pip could have a reduced entitlement in the future and would not say if the review's recommendations would lead to a reduced welfare bill.
sentences.article_title: Pip assessments need 'fundamental overhaul', report to say

sentences.text: The cost of Pip is expected to rise to more than £41bn by 2030, up from £15bn in 2020.
sentences.article_title: Pip assessments need 'fundamental overhaul', report to say

sentences.text: It was being claimed by 4m people in the UK as of 30 April 2026, according to the Department for Work and Pensions.
sentences.article_title: Pip assessments need 'fundamental overhaul', report to say

sentences.text: Though reforming the benefit has frequently been looked at as a way to reduce the Treasury's welfare bill, disability charities have described it as a lifeline for many.
sentences.article_title: Pip assessments need 'fundamental overhaul', report to say

sentences.text: Ahead of the Timms review being handed down, disability equality charity Scope said ministers must ensure Pip is not weakened.
sentences.article_title: Pip assessments need 'fundamental overhaul', report to say

sentences.text: "Life costs more when you're disabled, whether you work or not," executive director James Taylor said, adding that Pip was "vital financial support".
sentences.article_title: Pip assessments need 'fundamental overhaul', report to say

sentences.text: "We know there is real fear among disabled people that changes could leave them unable to afford the essentials." The disability benefit system is devolved in Scotland and will not change in line with England and Wales; however the Timms Review could impact the funding the Scottish government receives.
sentences.article_title: Pip assessments need 'fundamental overhaul', report to say

sentences.text: Disability benefits are also devolved in Northern Ireland, but in practice it reflects any changes made to the system in England and Wales.
sentences.article_title: Pip assessments need 'fundamental overhaul', report to say

sentences.text: Andy Burnham says he's "not persuaded" by the case for more powers The first minister says he wants an urgent meeting with the prime minister after Andy Burnham rejected calls to give more powers to the Welsh government.
sentences.article_title: Burnham does not view Wales as an equal nation, claims first minister

sentences.text: Rhun ap Iorwerth said he was "deeply disappointed" and that Burnham "does not view Wales as an equal nation".
sentences.article_title: Burnham does not view Wales as an equal nation, claims first minister

sentences.text: Meanwhile, Welsh Labour leader Ken Skates urged Burnham to "negotiate around a table" with ap Iorwerth.
sentences.article_title: Burnham does not view Wales as an equal nation, claims first minister

sentences.text: In a letter to ap Iorwerth last week, the prime minister said he was "not persuaded" by the case to devolve policing and justice , the Crown Estate and rail infrastructure to Wales.
sentences.article_title: Burnham does not view Wales as an equal nation, claims first minister

sentences.text: Welsh Secretary Stephen Kinnock said the UK government believed "devolution must be about more than transferring powers from one government to another".
sentences.article_title: Burnham does not view Wales as an equal nation, claims first minister

sentences.text: Trade union body TUC Cymru said it was disappointing calls for further devolution had been "dismissed without any discussion".
sentences.article_title: Burnham does not view Wales as an equal nation, claims first minister

sentences.text: In a written statement to Senedd members, the first minister said: "The refusal to even explore the devolution of the crown estate, justice and policing, and rail infrastructure proves that the prime minister does not view Wales as an equal nation.
sentences.article_title: Burnham does not view Wales as an equal nation, claims first minister

sentences.text: "The case in favour of Wales having control over these areas of responsibility – just like Scotland – is compelling.
sentences.article_title: Burnham does not view Wales as an equal nation, claims first minister

sentences.text: Several commissions have argued for the devolution of justice and policing, yet the UK government seemingly prefers to put unionist ideology before hard evidence.
sentences.article_title: Burnham does not view Wales as an equal nation, claims first minister

sentences.text: "This government is not interested in more powers for power's sake.
sentences.article_title: Burnham does not view Wales as an equal nation, claims first minister

sentences.text: The current settlement is unfair, unjust and unsustainable." Rhun ap Iorwerth is Plaid Cymru leader and first minister of Wales In a letter to the prime minister, ap Iorwerth asked the prime minister to reconsider the work of previous reports on the issue.
sentences.article_title: Burnham does not view Wales as an equal nation, claims first minister

sentences.text: He said he would "welcome an urgent meeting with you to discuss the evidence and agree a substantive way forward".
sentences.article_title: Burnham does not view Wales as an equal nation, claims first minister

sentences.text: Meanwhile, Welsh Labour leader Ken Skates called on the Welsh and UK governments to continue talks on the devolution of powers.
sentences.article_title: Burnham does not view Wales as an equal nation, claims first minister

sentences.text: He called for "greater detail" on why further devolution of policing was not happening, and said he will be meeting with Burnham himself.
sentences.article_title: Burnham does not view Wales as an equal nation, claims first minister

sentences.text: Welsh Labour has not dropped calls for the devolution of justice, the Crown Estate and rail investment.
sentences.article_title: Burnham does not view Wales as an equal nation, claims first minister

sentences.text: "You negotiate around a table," he said.
sentences.article_title: Burnham does not view Wales as an equal nation, claims first minister

sentences.text: "And you don't walk away when work needs to continue.
sentences.article_title: Burnham does not view Wales as an equal nation, claims first minister

sentences.text: Devolution is a process, not an event and Welsh Labour's position remains clear that we support further devolution to and within Wales." Skates continued: "Devolution of employment support is vital in getting to grips with the crisis of youth unemployment.
sentences.article_title: Burnham does not view Wales as an equal nation, claims first minister

sentences.text: The devolution of innovation funding will help strengthen the economy.
sentences.article_title: Burnham does not view Wales as an equal nation, claims first minister

sentences.text: "Devolution of youth justice will lead to better integration of youth services and social services and the justice system.
sentences.article_title: Burnham does not view Wales as an equal nation, claims first minister

sentences.text: "We need action as fast as possible in bringing these powers to Wales and in ensuring they go to the right people and places.
sentences.article_title: Burnham does not view Wales as an equal nation, claims first minister

sentences.text: "On policing, progress is being made, but I want greater detail over why full devolution is not happening as part of the current reforms." Meanwhile, TUC Cymru's general secretary, Laura Doel, said: "Our focus is on securing the powers and resources needed to improve outcomes for working people.
sentences.article_title: Burnham does not view Wales as an equal nation, claims first minister

sentences.text: That must include fair funding for Wales.
sentences.article_title: Burnham does not view Wales as an equal nation, claims first minister

sentences.text: "These are the long-established views of TUC Cymru and it's disappointing that our calls have been dismissed without any discussion.
sentences.article_title: Burnham does not view Wales as an equal nation, claims first minister

sentences.text: Prof Fiona Gilbert, who is co-leading the trial, will assess if AI can improve breast cancer diagnosis Nearly 700,000 women across the UK are to be invited to join the world's largest trial of how artificial intelligence can help in breast cancer screening.
sentences.article_title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out

sentences.text: AI will be used to review mammograms to see if it can improve early cancer detection and ease the workload of clinical staff, while not over-diagnosing women unnecessarily.
sentences.article_title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out

sentences.text: Recruitment to the EDITH trial , external has already begun at Cambridge University Hospitals, the first of 30 sites across the UK.
sentences.article_title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out

sentences.text: Women aged 50 to 71 are invited for routine breast screening every three years in the UK, and more than two million attend annually.
sentences.article_title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out

sentences.text: At present two NHS experts look at each breast X-ray, known as a mammogram, but in the trial, one of the human readers will be replaced by AI.
sentences.article_title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out

sentences.text: Several smaller studies have already shown that AI can improve breast cancer detection rates, but researchers running this trial say they need to be sure it won't cause harm by leading to women being recalled unnecessarily for further tests.
sentences.article_title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out

sentences.text: About a third of these are picked up by routine mammograms, usually at an early stage when they can be more easily treated.
sentences.article_title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out

sentences.text: It's estimated the screening programme helps prevent around 1,300 deaths a year.
sentences.article_title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out

sentences.text: Shirley Essex says routine breast screening saved her life Prof Fiona Gilbert, department of radiology, University of Cambridge, honorary consultant at Addenbrooke's Hospital, and co-chief investigator said: "Millions of women have a mammogram each year and only a small number, less than 1%, will have cancer.
sentences.article_title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out

sentences.text: Shirley Essex, 70, from Cambridgeshire, was diagnosed with early-stage breast cancer a year ago after a routine screening appointment.
sentences.article_title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out

sentences.text: She had surgery and radiotherapy, but did not require chemotherapy.
sentences.article_title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out

sentences.text: She told the BBC that her mammogram had saved her life: "I was astonished to be told I had cancer because I did not have any symptoms." Shirley is not part of the study but is passionate about the importance of screening.
sentences.article_title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out

sentences.text: "I feel so lucky my cancer was detected early.
sentences.article_title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out

sentences.text: It was my last routine mammogram, so if I had not attended, my cancer would have kept growing," she said.
sentences.article_title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out

sentences.text: Women will be informed about the study when they receive a routine screening invitation, but will not be obliged to take part.
sentences.article_title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out

sentences.text: The trial will not change what happens during a breast screening appointment.
sentences.article_title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out

sentences.text: Instead, it will test whether AI-assisted tools could replace one of the two human specialists reviewing mammograms.
sentences.article_title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out

sentences.text: Researchers say machine-learning software can be trained on millions of previous images in order to detect patterns, and so potentially find subtle changes in breast tissue that might be missed by the human eye.
sentences.article_title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out

sentences.text: In one arm of the trial, an AI programme will grade images before they are sent to NHS experts.
sentences.article_title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out

sentences.text: In another, it will review images afterwards.
sentences.article_title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out

sentences.text: The £10m trial is funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR).
sentences.article_title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out

sentences.text: It is being led by the University of Warwick, the University of Cambridge and Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, working with NHS England.
sentences.article_title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out

sentences.text: "Every scan will still be seen by a specialist, and if proven effective, it could ensure women get the diagnosis and treatment they need sooner," he said.
sentences.article_title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out

sentences.text: Four AI companies are involved in the trial, which is expected to last around three years.
sentences.article_title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out

sentences.text: Tracy and Kelvin Kane were jailed on charges connected with rioting in Ballymena in the summer of 2025 A mother and son described as ringleaders of rioting that targeted ethnic minorities have been jailed for what a judge called their "disgraceful activities".
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: Kelvin Kane, 32, of HMP Maghaberry, was jailed for four years on Monday after admitting 17 charges connected with rioting in Ballymena in the summer of 2025.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: His mother Tracy Kane, 51, of Galgorm Street in the town, was jailed for two years after admitting two counts including encouraging and assisting her son's crimes.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: Kelvin Kane's crimes included setting fire to a flat, which forced a family including a pregnant woman to be rescued.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: Antrim Crown Court was told Kelvin Kane was both an instigator and organiser of the first night of violent disorder in Ballymena on 9 June 2025, which the judge called "an orgy of violence".
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: Kelvin Kane's offences included one count of riot, seven of criminal damage and one of arson being reckless as to whether life was endangered.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: CCTV and police body-worn camera footage covering almost two hours was shown to the court at an earlier hearing on Thursday.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: It showed Kelvin Kane helping to build a barricade on the junction of Clonavon Road and Clonavon Terrace, throwing missiles including paint and bricks at police, kicking in or attempting to kick in the doors of houses and smashing the windows of properties.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: The court was also shown footage taken on a mobile phone from inside the ground floor flat of a property after Kane set fire to the kitchen.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: Judge Peter Irvine KC said a family from Bulgaria had to be rescued from the upstairs flat including a pregnant woman suffering from smoke inhalation and a young child.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: The court also viewed mobile phone footage taken by a family of eight adults and three children, including a three-year-old, who hid in the attic of a house in Clonavon Terrace for about four hours.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: Kelvin Kane broke the building's front window and attempted to kick down an internal door before entering the property, the court was told.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: Judge Irvine said the family, who were also from Bulgaria, were "clearly in a terrified state".
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: The court heard Kelvin Kane repeatedly targeted another property in Clonavon Terrace where a Filipino family lived, with the judge saying Kane seemed to find "particular satisfaction" attacking the home.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: The judge said Kelvin Kane was the first person to throw missiles and objects at police The judge said Kelvin Kane was the first person to throw missiles and objects at police.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: "I also find that you organised and orchestrated this riot," the judge said.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: "You are most certainly the leader and organiser and instigator of this particular series of disturbances that evening." On several occasions in the CCTV footage Kelvin Kane was seen with his arms in the air, which Judge Irvine said appeared to be "an act of gratuitous celebration".
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: The footage showed Tracy Kane at several points filming the disorder, speaking to her son and apparently pointing things out to him.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: Judge Irvine said she had done more than just assist Kelvin Kane, but had "instigated many of the events" and had been pointing out homes to him which were later attacked.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: The judge said Tracy Kane "may not have physically participated in the riot itself" but had instigated and encouraged her son's "disgraceful violent activities".
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: He described her as a ringleader who "led and directed a group of rioters concerned over a lengthy and sustained period of time".
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: He said Tracy Kane had clearly taken "great pleasure" in the disorder and referenced her being heard on video footage saying that the riot was "even better than the Twelfth of July".
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: A defence barrister for Kelvin Kane said his client deeply regretted his involvement in the rioting and admitted what he did was "entirely unjustified and wrong".
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: He said Kelvin Kane had "a significant and longstanding history of drug misuse and associated homelessness" and that his initial involvement "was not solely controlled, driven or motivated by race".
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: A barrister representing Tracy Kane said his client had a difficult upbringing and suffered from problems with alcohol.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: He said she felt genuine remorse and had made it clear to probation that her behaviour was "ridiculous".
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: Crowds clashed with police in Ballymena in June 2025 Judge Irvine said in a report compiled by an educational psychologist, Kelvin Kane had expressed "deep regret" and accepted he would have to accept the consequences for his actions.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: But he said Tracy Kane had "minimised her involvement" and had said she had become involved in the disorder out of a desire to protect her son.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: The judge said this was "unacceptable and inconceivable" and that Tracy Kane was not trying to protect him, but encourage him.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: "You are both a total and absolute disgrace to the decent law-abiding citizens of Ballymena," Judge Irvine said.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: "You are violent individuals and you both glorified in the racial hatred that was displayed that evening and directed towards the minority ethnic community.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: "Your behaviour must be utterly condemned by any sensible member of the public." He added that their offences were aggravated by racially hostility.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: Kelvin Kane was handed an eight-year sentence for the count of riot, with half to be served in prison and half on licence.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: He will serve it concurrently with sentences for the other 16 counts.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: Tracy Kane was handed a sentence of four years for the count of encouraging or assisting rioting, with half to be spent in prison and half on licence.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: She was also sentenced to 40 months for a count of burglary with intent to cause unlawful damage, with half to be spent in prison and half on licence.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: Both of her sentences will also run concurrently.
sentences.article_title: Mother and son riot ringleaders jailed for 'disgraceful' acts

sentences.text: Jurors have been shown CCTV footage of the attack Jurors have been sent out to begin considering their verdicts in the trial of a knifeman accused of attempting to murder 10 people on a London-bound train.
sentences.article_title: Jury out in train stabbing attempted murder trial

sentences.text: Anthony Williams, 33, stabbed 10 passengers between Peterborough and Huntingdon, Cambridgeshire, on 1 November 2025.
sentences.article_title: Jury out in train stabbing attempted murder trial

sentences.text: He has also pleaded not guilty to the attempted murders of three people in Peterborough and a boy in London prior to the stabbings.
sentences.article_title: Jury out in train stabbing attempted murder trial

sentences.text: After summing up the evidence in the case at Cambridge Crown Court, the judge, Mr Justice Calver KC, sent the jury out to start its deliberations.
sentences.article_title: Jury out in train stabbing attempted murder trial

sentences.text: It will resume on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: Jury out in train stabbing attempted murder trial

sentences.text: "You are under no time pressure whatsoever," he told jurors.
sentences.article_title: Jury out in train stabbing attempted murder trial

sentences.text: Williams has admitted wounding with intent to cause really serious bodily harm in respect of 12 victims and attempting to do so to two others.
sentences.article_title: Jury out in train stabbing attempted murder trial

sentences.text: Ten of the victims were stabbed on an LNER service from Doncaster to London King's Cross.
sentences.article_title: Jury out in train stabbing attempted murder trial

sentences.text: Williams is also accused of trying to murder three people in Peterborough the day before, as well as attempting to murder a boy in the early hours of 1 November on a train in east London.
sentences.article_title: Jury out in train stabbing attempted murder trial

sentences.text: In Court: Huntingdon Train Attack Follow all the developments from the trial as they unfold on our BBC podcast In Court The judge said jurors needed to ask themselves if they were sure the defendant "intended to kill" each victim.
sentences.article_title: Jury out in train stabbing attempted murder trial

sentences.text: He said psychiatrists instructed by the prosecution and defence agreed Williams "was suffering from an acute psychosis as a result of his schizophrenia" at the time.
sentences.article_title: Jury out in train stabbing attempted murder trial

sentences.text: The judge referred to statements allegedly made by Williams to a psychiatrist, including that he believed "people sent by the devil" wanted to attack him.
sentences.article_title: Jury out in train stabbing attempted murder trial

sentences.text: Calver said the psychiatrist also recalled the defendant saying that "during the events it was all real, he was attacking real people with real knives" and "I just needed to protect myself, it was me or them".
sentences.article_title: Jury out in train stabbing attempted murder trial

sentences.text: The judge said a "person who is mentally ill, acting psychotically under a delusion, can still form an intent to kill".
sentences.article_title: Jury out in train stabbing attempted murder trial

sentences.text: Anthony Williams boarded the train at Peterborough railway station Williams had made comments to people on the train including "do you want to die?" prosecutor Christopher Paxton KC said.
sentences.article_title: Jury out in train stabbing attempted murder trial

sentences.text: He said the defendant's alleged intention to kill "lay bare not just in his words... but in the slashes and stabs he inflicted not on the devil but on real people".
sentences.article_title: Jury out in train stabbing attempted murder trial

sentences.text: He noted Williams did not attack people on the platform before boarding the train.
sentences.article_title: Jury out in train stabbing attempted murder trial

sentences.text: "If there's a conspiracy by the devil, if it was Mr Williams saying, 'It's me or them', it's easier to kill people if they are trapped," Paxton said.

sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: A woman who is taking a civil case against her former church, over an allegation that she was groomed and sexually abused by a youth leader when she was a teen, has said she was failed by those who should have protected her.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: Jessica, not her real name, had been a member of a youth group in a Church of Ireland parish in County Antrim when she said she was first sexually assaulted at the age of 17 by a much older, married man.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: After she turned 18, she said she went on to become his "toy" and was coerced into months of what she described as non-consensual sex.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: The Diocese of Connor, which oversees Jessica's former church, said it would be "inappropriate" to comment on the allegations given the matter was the subject of legal proceedings.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: The alleged abuse happened about 20 years ago but a survivors' advocate warned that grooming continues to happen in faith settings, where young people are particularly vulnerable.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: Nikella Holmes, who is a survivor of sexual abuse and who supports others with similar experiences, said more learning was needed in churches in order to protect young people from potential predators.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: Jessica did not initially disclose her alleged abuse herself.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: It was the youth leader who told the County Antrim church that the pair had been having a consensual affair.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: Jessica said he had made the disclosure while he was under scrutiny for a separate unrelated issue, for which he was stood down from his youth leader role.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: According to Jessica, the church wrongly accepted this at face value and did not view his disclosure as a safeguarding issue.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: Years later, when she confronted a senior member of the church about how the matter was handled, she said they told her she had been viewed as someone who had been "groomed and taken advantage of".
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: Despite this, the church is defending Jessica's civil claim against it.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: Jessica is now in her 30s and after years of therapy and support from her loved ones said she was finally "in a good place".
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: But the abuse she said she was subjected to had left her a "broken, young girl" and, at one point, feeling suicidal.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: Jessica said that when the abuse began she had been having a hard time and that the youth leader offered her spiritual support and prayer.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: She said he was someone in a "position of authority", whom she "looked up to and trusted and respected".
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: "I believe he saw my vulnerability.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: He was witness to what was going on in my life and how I was struggling to cope with various things," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: "It was a crowded room full of people," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: "We were just watching TV at that point and the room was quite dark so no-one else was able to see.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: And he put his hand down my trousers and inside my underwear.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: I think I potentially stopped breathing for a few seconds.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: I was just in utter shock and couldn't feel my legs.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: My whole system literally shut down.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: "From then on I basically became his toy and he had such a hold over me that I just felt so stuck.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: Anything he said went." She said the sex that followed over the next number of months was not consensual.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: "When the other party isn't actively engaging, I would deem that as not wanting to take part, especially given his position in the church and the age gap," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: "He just had utter control over me and my movements and my life.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: I would have been out for a run, his car would have pulled up alongside me: 'Get in.'" Jessica said that as things progressed the youth leader told her he would kill himself if she told anyone.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: She said that with the "weight of his life" on her she kept the secret in order to "somehow protect him".
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: According to Jessica, her alleged abuse was not viewed as a safeguarding issue when the youth leader disclosed what he described as their relationship to senior members of the church.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: She said she was not asked at the time for her version of the events.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: "The leadership received information from one side and I think the information they got from that side was the easier version for them to potentially digest," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: "It was never regarded as a safeguarding issue.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: They claimed that I was an adult, throughout it all, that I was over 18, and that all activities were consensual from both parties." Shortly after the alleged abuse ended, Jessica said the church offered to pay for counselling and provided her with the name of a Christian counsellor.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: About a decade later, after she had processed her "trauma", Jessica said she approached a senior member of the church and asked "some hard, honest questions" about what was done in the aftermath of the alleged abuse.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: "The church had a duty of care to protect me, not only as one of their members but as a member of their youth, as a minor, essentially, when this all started," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: "And they didn't do that.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: And then later, as I went to them for help, they couldn't help me.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: They let me down." Jessica later reported her allegations to the Police Service of Northern Ireland, which pursued a criminal investigation, but she said the Public Prosecution Service chose not to prosecute given the years that had passed.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: The PPS told the BBC there was often a substantial period of time between the date of an alleged offence and the date of a person's first complaint, but that the "significant passage of time does not prevent the effective prosecution of sexual offences".
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: Jessica said she hoped that her civil case against her former church would help bring about change to the handling of safeguarding concerns.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: That was something Nikella Holmes said she believed was needed.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: Nikella was 15 when she was groomed and indecently assaulted two decades ago by a different youth leader at another church.
sentences.article_title: 'I was left broken' - Woman taking civil case against 'church that failed her'

sentences.text: She said church could be "all-consuming" for young people and when they seek guidance and support from their seniors who hold positions of trust and authority, they are particularly vulnerable, even after they turn 18.

sentences.text: The wife of disgraced comedian Russell Brand says she will "honour" the rules of his prison, a week after she read a message from her husband proclaiming his innocence.
sentences.article_title: Russell Brand's wife says she'll honour prison rules after message row

sentences.text: Laura Brand, 39, drew criticism from ministers after reading out the message from inside HMP Littlehey last week, prompting the government to seek to have the episode removed from social media platforms.
sentences.article_title: Russell Brand's wife says she'll honour prison rules after message row

sentences.text: She said on Sunday that she would continue to defend her family and herself over her portrayal in the media during the couple's weekly podcast, which she now presents alone.
sentences.article_title: Russell Brand's wife says she'll honour prison rules after message row

sentences.text: Russell Brand, 51, is currently serving a 10-and-half-year prison sentence after being convicted of rape and three counts of sexual assault.
sentences.article_title: Russell Brand's wife says she'll honour prison rules after message row

sentences.text: "Last week's episode drew a considerable amount of attention," Laura Brand said during this week's episode of Sunday Service.
sentences.article_title: Russell Brand's wife says she'll honour prison rules after message row

sentences.text: "Now that I understand the parameters set by the brilliant and professional staff at HMP Littlehey, I will absolutely honour that." In the relayed message last week, Russell Brand had said he was "not guilty of the offences I have been jailed for".
sentences.article_title: Russell Brand's wife says she'll honour prison rules after message row

sentences.text: Laura Brand said she had spoken to him at the Cambridgeshire prison and said he was "OK".
sentences.article_title: Russell Brand's wife says she'll honour prison rules after message row

sentences.text: Russell Brand was found guilty of raping a woman at his home in 2009, as well as three counts of sexual assault against three other women.
sentences.article_title: Russell Brand's wife says she'll honour prison rules after message row

sentences.text: Further allegations have since been reported about him and some have called for consent laws to be revised .
sentences.article_title: Russell Brand's wife says she'll honour prison rules after message row

sentences.text: His conviction has renewed conversation about safeguarding in the media industry, and whether some celebrities are still able to use their fame to prey on women and then silence them.
sentences.article_title: Russell Brand's wife says she'll honour prison rules after message row

sentences.text: Ministers have pointed out that inmates are prohibited from making statements that are likely to cause their victims distress and have said Brand's message was being investigated.
sentences.article_title: Russell Brand's wife says she'll honour prison rules after message row

sentences.text: A woman who alleges she was raped by Brand when she was 16, but who was not among the women whose accusations led to his conviction, said his prison message was "upsetting" and "really shocking" .

sentences.text: The government attempted to have the podcast removed from YouTube, but this was refused by its owner Google.

sentences.text: Shelly Magee and Clinton McKeever had hoped their son would be born in Newry A couple who are expecting their first child have said their excitement has turned  "into complete worry" because of the suspension of maternity services at their local hospital.
sentences.article_title: Woman faces hour-long drive to give birth as hospital suspends maternity services

sentences.text: Shelly Magee was due to give birth in Newry's Daisy Hill Hospital in County Armagh in January but from Monday, the Southern Trust is moving all hospital-based births to Craigavon, about 20 miles away.
sentences.article_title: Woman faces hour-long drive to give birth as hospital suspends maternity services

sentences.text: Her partner, Clinton McKeever, said the journey from their home in Mullaghbawn  could take them up to 90 minutes in bad weather or heavy traffic.
sentences.article_title: Woman faces hour-long drive to give birth as hospital suspends maternity services

sentences.text: The Southern Health Trust apologised to families facing longer journeys but said the shortage of obstetricians meant services must be temporarily concentrated at one hospital.
sentences.article_title: Woman faces hour-long drive to give birth as hospital suspends maternity services

sentences.text: "We mean it when we say it's temporary - we're going out to make further attempts to recruit," said its chief executive, Steve Spoerry.
sentences.article_title: Woman faces hour-long drive to give birth as hospital suspends maternity services

sentences.text: From Monday, all expectant mothers who receive treatment from the trust have been advised to go to Craigavon Area Hospital - not Daisy Hill - for all labour and birthing services, inpatient maternity care and emergency gynaecology support.
sentences.article_title: Woman faces hour-long drive to give birth as hospital suspends maternity services

sentences.text: It added that patients would receive the same high standard of care from experienced specialists, including staff from Daisy Hill who are relocating to Craigavon.
sentences.article_title: Woman faces hour-long drive to give birth as hospital suspends maternity services

sentences.text: Woman says 40-mile journey to hospital while having contractions was 'scary' Knock-on effects if maternity services suspended, trust chief says 'My son might not have survived without Daisy Hill maternity service' But the expectant couple have not been reassured by the trust's statements.
sentences.article_title: Woman faces hour-long drive to give birth as hospital suspends maternity services

sentences.text: Magee said Craigavon Area Hospital was "50 minutes from the house" by car.
sentences.article_title: Woman faces hour-long drive to give birth as hospital suspends maternity services

sentences.text: "A child doesn't choose a time to come," McKeever told BBC News NI.
sentences.article_title: Woman faces hour-long drive to give birth as hospital suspends maternity services

sentences.text: "To strip away a maternity service and claim it's for the safety of women is scandalous... there's no thought of safety in that journey." He said he was speaking from experience, having "had a taste of the journey already in a scenario that would be considered a crisis".
sentences.article_title: Woman faces hour-long drive to give birth as hospital suspends maternity services

sentences.text: About five years ago, his father suffered several broken ribs and a punctured lung in a fall.
sentences.article_title: Woman faces hour-long drive to give birth as hospital suspends maternity services

sentences.text: McKeever drove his father to Craigavon, having been advised by their local health clinic that it would take too long for an ambulance to get to Mullaghbawn.
sentences.article_title: Woman faces hour-long drive to give birth as hospital suspends maternity services

sentences.text: "The traffic was crazy and he felt every bump - I felt guilty for every bump.
sentences.article_title: Woman faces hour-long drive to give birth as hospital suspends maternity services

sentences.text: I got him there in the end but it was a very, very stressful journey," he recalled.
sentences.article_title: Woman faces hour-long drive to give birth as hospital suspends maternity services

sentences.text: "To know that I have to do it again with Shelly here, it's very concerning.
sentences.article_title: Woman faces hour-long drive to give birth as hospital suspends maternity services

sentences.text: It's took the excitement out of the whole thing and turned it into complete worry." To avoid having to drive to Craigavon in labour in January the couple are considering booking a hotel or rented accommodation near the hospital.

sentences.text: Despite their concerns, they praised their midwives in Newry and Crossmaglen, acknowledging staff also face uncertainty.

sentences.text: "I'd like to say to Clinton and Shelly that I'm really sorry it has come to this," Spoerry told the BBC's Good Morning Ulster programme .

sentences.text: "We wanted to maintain services at both hospitals, but our priority has, as they would expect, to be the safety of women and babies.

sentences.text: Ffion, Yugraj and Jessica say being ghosted has become a common part of applying for jobs Have you ever applied for a job or attended an interview, only to hear absolutely nothing back from the employer?
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: So-called "job ghosting" has become a big problem for jobseekers in the UK, leaving them "demoralised", denting their confidence and undermining their hopes of finding work.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: It's an issue that was mentioned in former minister Alan Milburn's major review into young people who are not in employment, education or training -  those dubbed as Neets - this week.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: Among his recommendations - aimed at reducing the proportion of Neets from 13% to about 5% by 2036 - Milburn proposed that large employers should give all unsuccessful job applicants under 25 "meaningful feedback".
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: The report's proposals relate mostly to England, with a recommendation that Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland adapt the principles to suit their own systems.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: But is feedback for all applicants realistic, given the vast number of applications these firms receive?
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: And what can people do to improve their chances in such a tough job market?
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: Yugraj Samrai, 23, from Coventry is currently unemployed and says he has submitted hundreds of job applications since he graduated from his marketing degree in July.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: But 30 to 40% of the time he hears nothing back at all, which can make him "feel like a statistic, not a person".
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: He tells the BBC: "I understand there are very few graduate jobs available, but at least give me a response to say whether I'll progress onto the next stage or not." Ffion Johns, from Llanelli, has been unemployed since June and did not get an interview until September after submitting 70 applications.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: The 24-year-old says her biggest problem throughout the job-hunting process has been the lack of feedback about why she didn't get the job, so she knows what to fix next time.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: Sometimes she has even been ghosted after attending an interview.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: "With most of these roles I'm not getting a rejection.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: I'm just not hearing anything, which can be quite frustrating," she says.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: Research by head-hunting firm Robert Walters last year found 86% of UK job hunters said their applications had been ignored, with no response at all from the hiring organisation.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: The Milburn report , external says this "wall of silence" is especially hard on young people as it gives them "nothing to learn from".
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: It adds that "time and emotional investment" goes into their applications.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: "It can really take hours and hours, so it just feels even worse to not even have that be recognised," says Jessica Anderson, 21, from Swindon.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: Employers say they are being flooded with job applications in a very competitive jobs market and it can be hard to respond to all of them.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: And AI is adding to the problem, enabling applicants to submit large numbers of applications in the hope of improving their chances.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: But Meg Burton, a career coach based in Leeds, says firms should at the very least inform job applicants when they are unsuccessful and that AI could help achieve this.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: Candidates should also be given proper feedback if they reach the interview stage, she says.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: "It doesn't have to be hugely detailed, it's just some pointers on why they were unsuccessful and what they can learn from that experience going forward," she says.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: The government could choose to adopt the Milburn proposals and crack down on job ghosting.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: But it raises another question: if candidates began receiving significantly more rejections than before, could this itself have a demoralising effect?
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: Ellie McCrone, 20, from Northampton understands the concern but thinks hearing back and getting constructive feedback where possible is always best.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: Ellie says constructive feedback is always preferable to being ghosted "If you are applying for hundreds of jobs and never getting anything, I think something is going wrong...
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: You can't fix something unless you know what the problem is." There are things applicants can do to improve their chances and avoid ghosting, such as tailoring their CV to each job and not submitting "hundreds and hundreds of applications" that all look the same, Burton adds.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: Candidates should also never take being ghosted personally, she adds.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: "Not hearing back doesn't mean you aren't a great candidate.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: Put it down to experience and move on."
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of applications, no replies: Inside the job ghosting problem‌

sentences.text: Whether it's scrolling through endless choice, spotting fake reviews, or working out if a "deal" is a deal at all, Black Friday sums up a lot of online woes.

sentences.article_title: Can AI really help spot Black Friday deals? We put it to the test

sentences.text: We had a go ourselves a week ahead of the big day.
sentences.article_title: Can AI really help spot Black Friday deals? We put it to the test

sentences.article_title: Can AI really help spot Black Friday deals? We put it to the test

sentences.article_title: Can AI really help spot Black Friday deals? We put it to the test

sentences.article_title: Can AI really help spot Black Friday deals? We put it to the test

sentences.text: Sophie Hope's credit score was hit by identity fraud Getting approval for a mortgage, a car loan or even a mobile phone contract can rest on a credit score.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Sophie Hope was on the sharp end of just such a decision.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "When I first checked my credit score, it was excellent.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: But then my mortgage application was suddenly denied by the lender because of my credit report.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: It was a massive shock as I'd never had bad credit.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: When I looked into it, my score had gone to 'very poor'," she says.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: It turns out, the Brighton-based nail technician and content creator, had been the victim of identity fraud.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "Someone had opened accounts in my name across various catalogue sites and ordered multiple items, including a PlayStation 4 and Nike socks," she says.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "Without me knowing, the debt was transferred to a secondary finance company.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: It spent three to four years accumulating in the background.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: It was only when I went to apply for a mortgage that I discovered how severely it had dragged down my credit score," she says.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Credit scores are "backward looking" says Funmi Olufunwa Hope's experience shows how crucial a credit score can be, but, as in her case, it does not tell the full story.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "As a nation, we are overly obsessed with credit scores," says Funmi Olufunwa, a consumer finance lawyer and founder of financial education business, Hoops Finance.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Three firms - Experian, Equifax and TransUnion - produce credit scores in the UK, and they all work from roughly the same data.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "A credit score is backward looking.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: It's looking at what has happened in the past, which doesn't necessarily predict the future," says Olufunwa.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "But when somebody's looking to lend you money, they're looking at what actually is affordable," she says.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Traditional credit scoring systems also disadvantage "thin-file applicants" - young people and recent immigrants to the UK who won't have built up a credit history.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: But with more financial data available than ever before - and a growing appetite for AI to make sense of it - could artificial intelligence help lenders work out who is safe to lend to?
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: In the US lending decisions will often hinge on a credit score from a company called FICO, which uses data from the big three credit assessment firms.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: But AI-powered lending firms, Upstart and Zest AI have both built businesses which offer lenders an extra option when it comes to assessing a client's credit worthiness.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "Thanks to our machine-learning models that look at more than 2,500 variables, we believe we can make significantly more loans at low prices to borrowers from every demographic group," Upstart said in statement.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: But like with many other applications of AI into everyday life, there are concerns.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "Consumers need to understand what information is being used to make decisions about them, and they need to be able to challenge something when it is wrong," Tucker explains.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Credit scores have been a contentious topic for decades for this very reason, says Sandra Wachter, professor of Technology and Regulation at the University of Oxford.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "We are not assessing if past decisions were right," Wachter argues, adding, AI does not know about existing social inequalities that impact decisions and could just "replicate what it has seen in the past".
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: While companies like Upstart and Zest AI see technology as a tool for financial inclusion, Wachter believes that real transformation requires accountability, as well as automation.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: She stresses that firms must apply existing regulations and establish new guardrails to ensure that AI does not simply perpetuate the biases of the past.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "Not putting any safeguards in place will fortify, foster, and enhance discrimination." Upstart says it is tackling that issue.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "We've invested in creating objective, automated evaluations to identify bias, and we've incorporated those evaluations into our model training process so it evolves to become even more accurate and more fair over time," the company said in a statement.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Evangeline Atkinson (left) and Laura Mills co-founders of Noggin HQ Evangeline Atkinson had a frustrating experience over her credit score.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "I was at university, paying rent, paying bills, as I had been doing for many years.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: I tried to get a £30-a-month phone contract, and they said no," she recalls.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "When I dug into it, it was because I was completely invisible to the system.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: No record could be found for me at any of the big three credit reference agencies." That experience inspired her to try to change the system.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: In 2021, Atkinson founded a credit reference agency with her best-friend from school, who had also experienced difficulties getting credit.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Their firm, Noggin HQ, was authorised by the FCA in June.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Atkinson explains it was set up to help consumers access affordable credit by analysing their current account transactional data.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: The platform helps lenders interpret thousands of individual data points about a person's spending habits.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Crucially, it does this without using AI, which Atkinson has also argued "carries the risk of inbuilt bias".
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "You have to be very careful", she warns.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "It's very sensitive data and it would be very easy for the models to be inferring various kind of protected characteristics." Experian announced a partnership with OpenAI in August Perhaps conscious of change, the big three credit scoring firms have all started experimenting with AI.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Equifax launched a platform called Equifax Amplify AI, which it says uses machine learning to sharpen credit assessment and fraud detection.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Meanwhile, in March TransUnion announced it was integrating Google's Gemini models "within its proprietary analytic data assets".
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: As for the future of credit scoring, companies are starting to look beyond traditional methods, according to consumer finance lawyer Funmi Olufunwa.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "They are beginning to realise that traditional credit scoring is inherently backward-looking, and that there are better predictors of the future out there." Whether consumers will be happy with AI playing a part in working out their future credit ratings is another thing.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Any change might be led by the younger, tech-savvy generation.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "They feel comfortable with their data being used this way, simply because it's the world they've grown up in.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "I wonder if older cohorts, who may not use technology as much, will be quite as comfortable with it," says Olufunwa.
