sentences.text: Photonic chips use light instead of electrons to process data "Photonic chips are on the verge of a breakthrough," says Ton van Mol of the Dutch research institute TNO.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: If van Mol is right – and TNO, the European Union and the Dutch government are backing the idea with millions of euros - then the technology could be a gamechanger.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: The chips which run today's society, from your phone and TV, to the vast data centres meeting our insatiable desire for AI, are mostly electrical.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: They process data by shunting electrons around tiny circuits – a single microchip produced today can contain billions of transistors, and sizes are measured in nanometres (one nanometre is a billionth of a metre).
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Because they use light instead of electricity, photonic chips are faster, use less energy and generate less heat than traditional computer chips.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Van Mol hopes for an acceleration in photonics similar to the one seen in electrical chips since the 1970s.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "With optical chips, you are now where electronic chips were maybe 40 [or] 50 years ago." American, Taiwanese and Chinese firms dominate the computer chip industry, but Europe sees the emergence of photonic chips as a fresh opportunity to lead, on what could be, a key future technology.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Which is why the European Union has committed €400m ($450m; £330m) to a project called PIX Europe , external , with the stated goal of making the continent "a global leader in emerging technology for Photonic Integrated Chips".
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "Europe said 'we need to have our own manufacturing in-house'," says van Mol, who is leading a key part of the programme.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Factories with machines that can handle bigger wafers can churn out chips more efficiently.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "[Photonic chip] manufacturing worldwide is [currently] done on wafers which are four inches (10cm) in size, and the next step is to scale-up production to a six-inch wafer," says van Mol.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: His team are already building a 10,000 sq m factory to produce six-inch indium phosphide wafers on the High Tech Campus in the Dutch city of Eindhoven.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: It's due to fully open in 2030 and will be a major step forward, not just for photonics in Europe, but around the world, according to van Mol.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "That's the development TNO is going to do, in a pilot line which is really serious.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: The Netherlands-based tech giant is the only company in the world able to build the machines needed to make the most sophisticated semiconductors.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Which is why ASML products will sit at the heart of the pilot line in Eindhoven - it's no coincidence that van Mol's project is based around the corner from ASML's headquarters.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "The way you produce these [photonic] chips is very similar to the way you produce electrical or electronic chip," says van Mol.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "You use the same type of equipment, you also need a high-end clean room, you also use wafers, so the production method is very similar to the traditional semiconductor technology." ASML itself is keen to explore the opportunities that the emerging technology of photonics could offer.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "Europe has a strong position in photonics research.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: The next challenge is translating those innovations into industrial-scale manufacturing," says Stanislas Baron, who is the head of ASML's EU/US Customer Team.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: The Eindhoven project has the backing of former ASML chief executive Peter Wennink, author of an influential report for the Dutch government called The Roadmap to Future Prosperity , external , which noted that the market for photonics was expected to grow 10 to 20 times in the next 10 years.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: In a news release backing the new pilot line, Wennink described it as "a launchpad for Europe's future digital economy".
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "By investing in scalable production capacity, we are creating an ecosystem that can help shape the global technological direction," he said.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Of course, Europe is not alone in looking to the potential of photonics to earn a global economic advantage.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: In June this year, US photonics company Coherent announced what it called "the world's first and largest volume-production six-inch indium phosphide manufacturing platform" at its plant in Sherman, in Texas.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: The expansion is backed by chip manufacturing giant Nvidia , external , as well as $50 million public funds under the US Chips Act.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: It's an illustration of how quickly the market is moving, and how central photonic chips could be to the continuing race to retain an influential stake in AI and technological development more generally.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Europe's bid to establish itself as a global leader in photonic chips – exemplified by the Eindhoven project – is the kind of strategy that makes sense in a globalised economy, says Joris Teer, policy analyst at the European Institute for Security Studies in Brussels.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: If the continent can take a lead in photonic chips, then future developments in AI and data will partly be dependent on Europe.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "Europe knows that its high energy and labour costs, skilled workforce shortages, and lack of private and public capital make an across-the-board reindustrialisation strategy impossible", Teer says.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "To retain influence, ensuring dependence on European parties rather than European autonomy is key." Once up and running, the Eindhoven project will provide a pilot production line which can be used multiple companies.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: It will be open to businesses across Europe and beyond, who can design and build chips without having to develop their own expensive production facilities.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "What we want to establish here is what we call a foundry model; there's no intention to have our own product," Ton van Mol says.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Instead, they will produce to order for outside customers.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: It's the same idea which, at huge scale, has brought Taiwanese-based giant TSMC a position of global dominance in the manufacture of microchips.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Photonic chips are already in use, in highly specialised areas in data centres and in Lidar (light detection and ranging) sensor technology, for instance.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: For van Mol of TNO, helping the industry to scale up, by easing production challenges and increasing capacity, is the key step to moving them into the tech we use in our daily lives, like phones and laptops, and to drive innovation in areas like medical scanners and 6G communications.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: A jet engine will have hundreds of turbine blades Every time you fly, an extraordinary feat of endurance occurs inside the aircraft's engines.

sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: And these hardy blades are not sculpted or cut from their material – they are grown.

sentences.text: During the 1960s, engineers worked out how to take a molten metal alloy, cast it into the shape of a turbine blade, and then cool it very carefully from one end to the other over a matter of hours.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: A single crystal or grain of metal alloy forms during this process of gradual, delicate solidification.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Like turning a cup of water into one big snowflake, of your own design, rather than a mini blizzard of many smaller snowflakes.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "It's about as complicated as manufacturing gets," says Ben Fifoot, manufacturing engineer at Rolls-Royce, which makes turbine blades in the UK.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "It's a real motivator to get out of bed in the morning." Only a handful of companies around the world can produce these single crystal turbine blades, and the process has been perfected end-to-end in just five countries, including the US and UK.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky at Downing Street last month The UK will provide Ukraine with 1,000 long-range strike drones to target Russia beyond the front line, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has announced.
sentences.article_title: UK to provide Ukraine with 1,000 long-range strike drones

sentences.text: The drone support was announced at a meeting in Berlin of Ukraine's allies, the Coalition of the Willing, and is part of a new £260m package to boost its war defences this winter.
sentences.article_title: UK to provide Ukraine with 1,000 long-range strike drones

sentences.text: The government said the drones are able to fly up to 625 miles (1,000km) and carry heavier warheads, enabling Ukraine to target military production facilities.
sentences.article_title: UK to provide Ukraine with 1,000 long-range strike drones

sentences.text: The move is the latest sign of a growing British involvement in drone technology for Ukraine.
sentences.article_title: UK to provide Ukraine with 1,000 long-range strike drones

sentences.text: The government said 80% of the package will be spent in the UK.
sentences.article_title: UK to provide Ukraine with 1,000 long-range strike drones

sentences.text: The Berlin talks came as US President Donald Trump is meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese Premier Xi Jinping.
sentences.article_title: UK to provide Ukraine with 1,000 long-range strike drones

sentences.text: Ahead of that meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation (Apec) summit in China, Trump said both he and Xi want to see an end to the Ukraine war.
sentences.article_title: UK to provide Ukraine with 1,000 long-range strike drones

sentences.text: Burnham, who co-chaired the meeting, had said the UK must do everything it can to make sure Ukraine can defend itself from Russian attacks throughout the winter.
sentences.article_title: UK to provide Ukraine with 1,000 long-range strike drones

sentences.text: Speaking at a press conference after the talks, Burnham said the mood of the coalition is "more determined than ever to stay the course" in support of Ukraine.
sentences.article_title: UK to provide Ukraine with 1,000 long-range strike drones

sentences.text: He welcomed the presence of US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff at the meeting and described Russia as "perhaps the biggest losers" of the conflict, as he referred to casualties they have suffered.
sentences.article_title: UK to provide Ukraine with 1,000 long-range strike drones

sentences.text: Burnham said: "This clearly has got to be a moment to move towards peace because of the US involvement that we've seen today and the progress clearly that is being made.
sentences.article_title: UK to provide Ukraine with 1,000 long-range strike drones

sentences.text: Meanwhile, Russian forces have been focused on knocking out power in Ukraine before winter with attacks on critical infrastructure.
sentences.article_title: UK to provide Ukraine with 1,000 long-range strike drones

sentences.text: The UK is among a number of countries also supplying Ukraine with lightweight missiles which are being used to intercept Russian jet-powered drones.
sentences.article_title: UK to provide Ukraine with 1,000 long-range strike drones

sentences.text: Ukraine's strike rate is now close to 70%, more than double what it was just a couple of months ago, Downing Street said.
sentences.article_title: UK to provide Ukraine with 1,000 long-range strike drones

sentences.text: The UK also pledged further air defence support this week and sanctioned Russia's 10 major oil producers.
sentences.article_title: UK to provide Ukraine with 1,000 long-range strike drones

sentences.text: Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said the government was delivering on a promise for more support for Ukraine at the Budget.
sentences.article_title: UK to provide Ukraine with 1,000 long-range strike drones

sentences.text: "Ukraine's frontline is the frontline for freedom and democracy, and we will stand with them for as long as it takes," he said.
sentences.article_title: UK to provide Ukraine with 1,000 long-range strike drones

sentences.text: Meanwhile, on Friday Burnham will head to Brussels for a UK-EU summit, where both sides hope to unveil new agreements on food, youth visas and re-linking British industry to the EU's carbon trading regime.
sentences.article_title: UK to provide Ukraine with 1,000 long-range strike drones

sentences.text: Sales of a baby sleeping bag have been halted in the UK by fashion retail chain Next, after a new mum raised the alarm over its safety.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: Emma Hunter, 29 from Norwich, contacted BBC Your Voice to say she realised the neck hole was far too big - meaning her daughter Rosie could potentially wriggle down, burying her face and risking suffocation.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: Emma recalls: "I woke up my husband and we both agreed there was no way we could put Rosie in it." Next says its own-brand, 2.5 tog pink floral sleep bag with removable sleeves that comes in three sizes, has been removed from the website and stores and a product recall is under way.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: Next will contact and advise customers who purchased the item from them.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: The sleeping bag is now unavailable on Next's website after safety fears were raised A spokesperson for Next said: "We can confirm the item has been removed from our website and all stores.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: A product recall is in place, and we are contacting all customers who purchased the item directly to advise them of the appropriate next steps." Emma says she started doing her own research that same night she realised the sleeping bag was unsuitable for Rosie.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: Although the product had a label stating that it met British standards, Emma discovered that the maximum neck circumference for that size of bag should be 32cm.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: When she measured the bag, the neck hole was 36cm.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: According to the British Retail Consortium (BRC), a significant hazard arises if a child slips through the neck opening of a sleep bag and the material covers the child's nose and mouth.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: They state that "suffocation can occur and may lead to the brain becoming starved of oxygen, which may result in asphyxia and potential brain damage or fatality." To limit this hazard, the EN 16781 standard specifies a maximum and minimum size for the neck opening circumference in relation to the child's height.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: For example, a sleep bag designed for a child 50 cm to 65 cm tall should have a minimum neck circumference of 28 cm and a maximum of 32 cm.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: Rosie, who is now three and a half months old, measured 59cm at the time the bag was bought.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: After flagging these issues to the company, Emma says she was surprised by their initial reaction.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: "They seemed quite laissez faire about it and just offered me a refund, but I said 'it's dangerous, surely you shouldn't be selling it any more and there should be a product recall?'" Emma was told by Next that they were looking into it and that their product team was examining the bag and would feed back.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: Emma's older brother died of Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS) as a baby so the risk to babies from suffocation is something close to her heart.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: She told the BBC: "I am more aware of this because of what happened to my brother and my family, but it shouldn't take an infant mortality to see change.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: "They didn't have any sense of urgency about it at all and I expected a big high street store like that to have a certain standard.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: You put your trust into these retailers.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: "How can a product have a label on it saying it met the British standard, when it clearly didn't?" Ruth Watts, who is a qualified health visitor in England, says that babies will differ in terms of size and height, despite their age.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: But if a sleeping bag covers the chin or face in any way it should not be used.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: "The best thing to do is check the gap around the neck.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: If you can fit one to two fingers around the neck then that's safe.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: If it's any tighter or looser than that, then you shouldn't use it," she recommends.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: Emma's baby Rosie is now 3 and a half months old and uses a different sleeping bag The Lullaby Trust is a UK charity that works to prevent sudden, unexpected infant deaths, including SIDS.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: CEO Jenny Ward told BBC News that the charity could not comment on the safety of specific products, since it does not carry out independent product safety testing.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: But she encourages families to check that any product they use has passed the necessary safety checks and meets British Safety Standards.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: She said: "Remember to follow the manufacturer's instructions and if a family is worried about any product  we would say to stop using it and contact the manufacturer.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: "We support the Office for Product Safety and Standards' recent warning on certain baby sleep bags and would urge families to ensure a sleep bag fits well before they use it." People can check if any products have been recalled by visiting the OPSS website , external .
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: CT scans before (left) and after treatment with daraxonrasib plus chemotherapy (gemcitabine and nabpaclitaxel) showing multiple tumours that are no longer visible.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Yellow arrows indicate the tumours visible before treatment Experts are calling it the biggest breakthrough in pancreatic cancer treatment for decades - a daily pill that appears to shrink and possibly even eliminate tumours in some patients with one of the deadliest and hardest-to-treat cancers.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Cancer became undetectable on scans in one in 12 of the patients given daraxonrasib along with chemotherapy in early medical trials.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Tumours stopped growing in almost all of the 61 participants who had recently been diagnosed with advanced pancreatic cancer that had spread to other parts of the body.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: But doctors stress it is unclear how long it might keep the disease at bay and should not be seen as a cure.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Cancer Research UK called it "the biggest leap forward in decades" for pancreatic cancer patients.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: The charity's Dr Sam Godfrey told BBC News that the results were incredibly exciting.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: "What this new drug has done is it's found a way of drugging the undruggable.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: "We are finally seeing progress in pancreatic cancer which is so long overdue." Pancreatic cancer is notoriously hard to treat and has the lowest survival rate of all common cancers in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Although chemotherapy can shrink tumours a bit, the cancer often grows again.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Most patients with advanced disease survive months, not years.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Doctors hope the new treatment might offer patients more time, even if it cannot stop cancers for good.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: The trial followed patients for a year and a half, on average, and some did not see their cancer return during this time.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: "We are beginning to see not only a higher percentage of tumour response rates, but also deeper responses and a near doubling in the duration of disease control, which may eventually translate into longer survival," he said.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Daraxonrasib is a targeted inhibitor treatment that has already been approved in the US .
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: It works by locking on to and shutting off certain mutations, called RAS , external , found in most pancreatic cancers that drive tumour growth.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Dozens of other cancers, including lung and ovarian, can have similar mutations, meaning the drug might help lots of other patients too.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Dr Godfrey said: "I would hope that the early success that we are beginning to see in pancreatic cancer can also be rolled out to other cancers." He said longer trials and results were vital.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: In Britain, there are 11,500 diagnoses of the disease each year and around 10,200 deaths, according to Cancer Research UK.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Actor Alan Rickman died of the disease in 2016, five months after diagnosis.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Symptoms can include , external jaundice, itchy skin, darker pee, paler poo, unexplained weight loss, tiredness and high temperature.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: More than 200 doctors have had their details sent in error to the Times newspaper The doctors' regulator the General Medical Council (GMC) has apologised after it mistakenly sent information about more than 220 doctors to a national newspaper.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The information included summaries of complaints alleging antisemitism or Islamophobia against the doctors.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: For some of the medics involved, it was only when the GMC alerted them to the data breach that they discovered a complaint had been made about them.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The GMC says it is "very sorry" for the incident and has reported itself to the Information Commissioner's Office.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The GMC - an independent body that regulates doctors, physician associates and anaesthesia associates to protect patient safety - sent the information about 223 doctors to a journalist at the Times newspaper.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: While no names were revealed, GMC identification numbers were included, which would easily allow doctors to be found on the regulator's register.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: Some doctors have also raised concerns that their ethnicity was included in the data breach.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: All the medics involved have been the subject of a complaint involving either antisemitism or Islamophobia, dating from the Hamas attack on Israel in October 2023 to September 2026.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The GMC says it has a legal and statutory responsibility to investigate such claims.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: Meanwhile, the Times is understood to have promised not to make any of the  details public, but has said it will not delete the information.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: A spokesman for the doctor's trade union, the British Medical Association (BMA), condemned the release of personal information.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: "The BMA is aware that a number of doctors have received communication from the GMC to say that it erroneously sent personal identifiable data about them to the Times newspaper when responding to a media request," it said.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: "The GMC must take action to ensure such a breach never occurs again." The BMA said it would look at ways to support members affected and urged them to make contact via their website.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: A doctors' campaign group, The Doctors' Association UK (DAUK), called for an independent investigation into the error.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: "If a doctor sent identifiable patient information to a newspaper, they could expect to be referred to the GMC," said Dr Matt Kneale, DAUK co-chairman.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: "The GMC should hold itself to the same standard of confidentiality it expects from doctors.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: Just over a quarter of complaints over Islamophobia - 26% - have led to disciplinary action.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: But other complaints were closed, having failed to reach the threshold for investigation.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The GMC said it had contacted the doctors affected to explain what had happened, to apologise and provide information and support.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: A spokesperson added: "We recognise the concern this will cause to both those impacted personally and other registrants and we are very sorry this happened.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: "Our priority continues to be supporting those affected and taking steps to reduce the impact of this incident." Clarification 20 November: This article was amended on 19 November to remove references to the information being 'leaked'.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The information was mistakenly disclosed by the GMC in response to a media request.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: Early efforts to contain coronavirus "were doomed to fail" because the test, trace and isolate system in the UK could only handle a relatively small number of cases, the seventh report of the Covid inquiry says in a damning assessment.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Across 245 pages the inquiry looks at everything from border controls to how well contact tracing worked.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Here's what you need to know.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The report said the virus was allowed to spread virtually unchecked in the first few months after community testing and contact tracing was abandoned in mid-March 2020, costing lives.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Ministers said this was because testing capacity was being overwhelmed.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: NHS Test and Trace was launched two months later and eventually became one of the biggest testing services in the world per head of population.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: In the end, more than £30bn was spent across the UK during the pandemic on testing, tracing and isolating.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Once established, it was effective.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: But in those early months the four UK nations were "effectively blind" to how quickly Covid was spreading, the inquiry said.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: It criticises the government for not having a robust test, trace and isolate system in place to start with, saying this, alongside other failures, meant harsher measures, including lockdown and school closures, were needed.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Inquiry chair Baroness Hallett said the UK should have been better prepared and learnt lessons from other countries that had experience of dealing with outbreaks of other infectious diseases, such as Sars.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Unlike the UK, places such as Hong Kong, South Korea, Singapore and Taiwan had established systems ready to go.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: This was despite the fact the UK had run a series of simulation exercises in the years leading up to Covid.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: They included Exercise Cygnus into a flu pandemic and Exercise Alice into Mers.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Both identified problems relating to test, trace or isolation, which appear not to have been fully acted on.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The report also raises the question of whether the government could have made use of non-government testing facilities in hospitals, universities and the private sector from the start, instead of just relying on 12 government labs.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: When people in the UK were told to isolate, "many felt forgotten and let down by the lack of practical or financial support when trying to follow the rules", says the report.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: In the early months of the pandemic, estimates suggested less than half of people were complying with the rules around isolating if infected.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Ministers and their advisers discussed this and fines of up to £10,000 were introduced for those who did not comply, which some experts have said was counter-productive.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Changes were made to allow people to claim statutory sick pay.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: But it was not until September in England – and later in Scotland and Wales – that £500 financial payments were introduced to help those on low incomes comply.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: More also needed to be done to provide practical support for things such as collecting medicines and shopping for food for those who did not have people to call on.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Suspending all flights from China to the UK in February 2020 could "have provided valuable additional time to prepare healthcare systems for the impact of the pandemic", said inquiry chair Baroness Hallett.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The report says the UK lacked a clear strategy for implementing border control measures early in the pandemic, which left the country in an "extremely vulnerable position".
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: By contrast, the UK government only requested travellers arriving from high-risk areas to self-isolate for 14 days.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The UK government implemented no further border control measures until June 2020.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The report says that border controls were a "critical gap in the UK's ability to limit the spread of the virus" and recommends that in the future "international border control measures should be in place at the earliest stages of a pandemic".
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The inquiry report is more positive about the use of smartphone apps, saying digital tools can have a "significant impact on reducing the spread of infection".
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: It quotes a mathematical modelling study from the US which estimates that, when 75% of people used a contact tracing app in the pandemic, infections were reduced by at least 50%.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Three different apps were developed during Covid - one for England and Wales, another for Scotland and a third for Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The inquiry says that took up "valuable time", and it recommends developing a UK-wide digital tool to use in any future outbreak.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: It says it is "fundamentally important" that apps and digital tools are as accurate as possible – and people have confidence in them.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: In the summer of 2021, as Covid restrictions were relaxed, around 7% of all UK adults were told to self-isolate over a seven-day period, something dubbed by the press as the "pingdemic".
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: It quotes Treasury estimates suggesting that may have reduced economic growth by as much as 0.3% that month.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The government has set out a timetable for when the leasehold system in England and Wales will be dismantled.
sentences.article_title: Timetable set out for dismantling leasehold system in England and Wales

sentences.text: Under the plans, most new flats - with only limited exemptions - will be sold as commonhold, where residents collectively own and manage their buildings.
sentences.article_title: Timetable set out for dismantling leasehold system in England and Wales

sentences.text: Adverts for tests and services relating to low testosterone are allowed but must be rooted in evidence, the regulator said Five adverts by online healthcare provider Voy have been banned by the watchdog for making misleading claims linked to low testosterone in men.

sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: "The problems London faces are the symptoms.

sentences.text: Andy Burnham has hailed his deal with the EU as a "good day for Britain" and a "good day for Europe".
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: In the hours before the prime minister spoke, it had become, if nothing else, a confusing day.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: That confusion was unleashed by an EU official who briefed reporters in the morning that implementing the new arrangements on youth mobility, food exports and carbon emissions would be contingent on the government agreeing within six months to cut university tuition fees for Europeans studying in Britain.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: That was later qualified by others in the EU - and straightforwardly disputed by the British government.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: And for all that it dominated the morning, it did not ultimately dominate or particularly overshadow what was a warm press conference between the prime minister and his EU counterparts, Ursula von der Leyen and Antonio Costa.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: The settled position appears to be that negotiations on student fees will continue into the next six months but on a separate track, or a "different sheet of paper" as von der Leyen put it.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: This still carries some degree of political risk for Burnham, because if Britain agrees to reduce, let alone equalise, university fees that would be an economic hit for universities which would presumably end up being covered by the government.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: And it may still be possible, though probably unlikely, that a deterioration in those negotiations could pollute the progress of today's agreements.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: Conversely, expect Burnham and his ministers to talk up another area where negotiations will continue - on the UK not being affected by the EU's "Made in Europe" plans, an attempt by the bloc to protect its industries from Chinese competition.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: Today's achievements and hiccups alike may quickly pale into insignificance anyway.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: UK and EU agree new deal for food exports, youth mobility and emissions but student fee talks to continue Faisal Islam: This cost-cutting UK-EU deal doesn't mean lower prices will follow What is the EU-UK youth experience scheme and when will it start?
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: At the dramatic conclusion of his first party conference speech as Labour leader in September - a moment he has been dreaming of for decades - the prime minister vowed to get closer to the EU.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: Over the subsequent two months it has at times been a bit unclear how exactly he envisages that playing out and quite how far he is willing to go.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: But focusing on the process risks obscuring the most important development, which is that the prime minister and the government are now unambiguously committed to Britain not only getting closer, but getting much closer to the EU.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: There were two significant moments at today's summit in that regard.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: First, Burnham said that the government had got as far as it could go with incremental deals with the EU, at least this side of a general election.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: In other words, he has got as far as he believes is possible with the strategy he inherited from Sir Keir Starmer of getting closer to the EU within the confines of the post-Brexit architecture set out by Theresa May all those years ago, of Britain remaining outside the single market and the customs union.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: That suggests that after two years of this, there will not be a third annual summit to unveil specific agreements designed to smooth post-Brexit issues affecting specific sectors.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: Yet it does sound like there will be another summit next year - or, rather, an "informal brainstorming process" about potential options for future relations with the EU.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: That sounds pretty nebulous, sure, but an event dedicated specifically to both sides discussing how to change the terms of Britain's arrangements with the EU is likely to become quite a big moment when it arrives.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: Perhaps as importantly, von der Leyen made clear that the EU was embracing this event too.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: That said, it does diminish the chances of major movement from Burnham towards embracing a specific model for the EU relationship in the intervening period.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: And what of the domestic politics of this?
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: Britain's seventh prime minister in just over 10 years watched from Manchester as the fraught relationship with Europe wrecked the careers of so many of those predecessors.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: Burnham's gamble is that this time it's different.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: He believes that public regret about how Brexit has played out opens the political space for a far-reaching renegotiation.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: Plenty of Labour MPs enthusiastically agree, and see this as the route to uniting the "progressive" vote at the next election too.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: Some, especially those who represent Labour's former industrial heartlands, are a little more apprehensive.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: This morning's confusion is a reminder that there is another element to this gamble.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: Negotiating with Brussels, even if both sides believe progress is a "win-win", can be a fraught and complicated business.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: Once he's on the other side of his brainstorm, can Burnham carry that off without getting bogged down and distracting from his government's other priorities?
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: On the day he became Labour leader in July, Burnham described it as the biggest change moment in British politics in 40 years.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: He was talking principally about economic transformation.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: But going to Brussels and getting what he wants without serious complications would be a pretty big change too.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: From Spring 2027, under 16s will no longer be able to access several social media applications More than 300,000 young people in Britain will work with researchers to help understand how the UK's forthcoming social media ban for under-16s could affect mental health.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: The studies will examine the habits of the children and teenagers, including whether they spend less time on their phones and what they are replacing scrolling with.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Ten different projects have been commissioned, taking place across England, Wales and Scotland, to help reflect a diverse range of teenagers.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: The social media ban, beginning in spring 2027, will follow a similar model to that already introduced in Australia to stop children accessing platforms such as Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Apps such as Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, Snapchat and YouTube will be banned under new rules The work, funded by health charity The Wellcome Trust, will help inform future online safety policies in the UK and internationally, with some early results available before the ban happens.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Researchers will use wearable technology, smartphones, digital diaries and surveys to collect data to see how young people respond to the ban, both physically and mentally.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: And they will check whether young people find ways to circumvent restrictions.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Dr Camilla Iannone, research lead at Wellcome, said it was a once-in-a-generation opportunity to study at scale how social media and its restrictions affected youth mental health.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: "We really don't think that this is a simple binary question of whether social media is good or bad, or whether restrictions work or don't work.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: "Instead, the teams will study whether changing young people's digital environment leads to meaningful changes in their mental health and wellbeing." Participants are being recruited to reflect a diverse range of young people, including different genders and sexual orientations.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: People with existing mental health conditions, such as anxiety and depression, will also be included, as well as young people who are neurodivergent.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Groups have been set up at Cardiff University, the University of Oxford, the University of Birmingham, King's College London, the University of Edinburgh, the University of Manchester, the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, and University College London.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: This video can not be played 'When I found out about Breast Friends it was the best thing ever' Annette Farrington-Moore says a charity became a lifeline after her breast cancer diagnosis, and now the group that helped her is celebrating a major milestone with a royal seal of approval.

sentences.text: Run by volunteers with lived experience of the disease, Breast Friends Solihull provides emotional and practical support with many involved forging lifelong friendships.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "You don't want to trouble family and they don't really understand what you're going through emotionally," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "The kids were there for me but when I found out about Breast Friends it was like the best thing ever." Those who run the group firmly believe that no-one should go through breast cancer alone.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: The organisation has supported thousands of people affected by breast cancer over the last 25 years, and has juar been awarded the King's Award for Voluntary Service.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: Annette Farrington-Moore was diagnosed with breast cancer in January 2025 Annette, 64, was diagnosed with breast cancer last year.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: Widowed and feeling low, she found solace in attending meetings and events put on by the group.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "Whenever you're ill and you haven't got your husband, there's no one there to look after you like they would," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "So having Breast Friends, you know there's somebody on the end of the phone who can be there for you." The charity provides services such as gardening and cleaning to allow people to rest during treatment, as well as support with bras, wigs and hospital visits.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: It has also raised money to fund hospital equipment.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: The charity's committee members say they believe in prescribing a healthy dose of laughter and friendship Chris Pile was diagnosed with breast cancer 20 years ago, when she was a nurse and mother of two young children.

sentences.text: She is now vice-chair of the group and helps lift others when they're down.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "I joined Breast Friends when I finished my chemotherapy and radiotherapy, and I found it really uplifting," she explained.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: Everybody was so positive and friendly, and I got involved straight away because that's the kind of person I am.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "I've organised days and nights out, summer suppers and the Christmas dos." Now vice-chair of the group, Chris Pile was diagnosed with breast cancer 20 years ago Chair Deborah Douglas has had breast cancer twice, first in 2003 and again earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: She said she has now been given "the all clear" following treatment.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: Her experiences mean she knows first-hand what support to offer, explaining that a diagnosis can be "scary and frightening".
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: Chair of Breast Friends Deborah Douglas said achieving the Kings Award for Voluntary Service meant more people would hear about the group and ask for help Her first diagnosis led her to seek help from Breast Friends.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "I walked in and I saw women who weren't sad.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: They were all happy and so uplifting, and they basically supported me from the moment I walked in.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "It was such an uplifting experience, and I always leave Breast Friends smiling," she added.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "We laugh, but we also talk about our issues and how we're feeling.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "That emotional support is so important because the people around you know exactly what you're going through.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: People don't always want to share those things with their family." More than 20 years on, she is still involved as the group's chair.

sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: A six-in-one vaccine given to young children - also known as the DTaP/IPV/Hib/Hep B vaccine - offers protection against diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, hepatitis B, polio and Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib).
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: The government has warned some schools start teaching GCSEs in the first year of secondary school Secondary schools will be told not to teach GCSEs early as part of a major shake-up of how children in Years 7 to 9 are taught in England.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The government plans to make Key Stage 3 a more distinct education phase, urging schools to focus less on exams and more on a "richer, more engaging" experience.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The changes come in response to two reviews that found pupils were increasingly becoming disengaged in their early teenage years, affecting attendance and achievement, the Department for Education (DfE) said.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The move will mark a reversal of the approach taken by the previous Conservative government to focus the first three years of secondary school on core subjects and on doing well in assessments.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: Former Education Secretary Michael Gove prioritised English, maths and science, while raising grade boundaries, making exams harder and limiting resits.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: He also made GCSEs linear, meaning they are sat all in one go at the end of Year 11 instead of over the course of Key Stage 4.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: These reforms meant teachers started preparing pupils for exams at an earlier stage at the expense of teaching unexamined parts of their subject.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The DfE has pledged a "more engaging offer" in subjects like drama, PE, music and languages, which have seen a decline in students taking them, when it publishes its new curriculum later this year.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: It says persistent absence nearly doubles among pupils between Year 6 and Year 9.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The department pointed to a recent survey commissioned by the International Baccalaureate that found GCSE prep dominated Key Stage 3 learning in England, with 57% of teachers saying it was the leading influence on the curriculum.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: "The pressures of GCSEs and an overcrowded curriculum are resulting in too many children receiving a narrower offer during Key Stage 3 and being rushed towards exams without grasping the fundamentals or developing deeper understanding," Powell said.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: "I'm putting a stop to that." A 2015 Ofsted report suggested that Key Stage 3 may be "wasted years", echoing the view at the time that pupils aged 11-14 lacked a clear motivation to work hard.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: However, the government faced criticism at the time that its reforms made each exam far more significant, meaning teachers refocused lessons only on what could come up in them.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: Reacting to the DfE's announcement on Sunday, Lib Dem education spokeswoman Munira Wilson MP said school was "more than drilling kids for exams" but cautioned against "micromanaging" teachers.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: She added that a new curriculum "alone won't get children back into the classroom", noting that "too many pupils are missing school because of anxiety and unmet mental health needs" while "schools can't offer more drama, music and languages without the teachers to teach them".
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: Alan Milburn has said the country needs a "complete system reset" to bring down the number of young people not in work or education - known as "Neets".
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: In a major review, published on Tuesday, , external he suggested a raft of proposals to address the problem, which mostly cover England but he says can be adapted in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland too.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Each of his recommendations will need to be accepted by the government and implemented and paid for before they become reality - and that could take some time.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: So how might today's proposals affect you if you are Neet?
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Major report proposes welfare changes, apprenticeships and tax cuts to help 440,000 young people into work At the heart of the recommendations, Milburn says, is a new Youth Opportunity Service.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: He wants this to be implemented locally, with each area drawing up a plan to help their own young people.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: It would bring together employment, careers, health and practical support, with each young person getting a named adviser and a personalised plan.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn wants areas to begin building their Youth Opportunity Service from 2027, with one in place everywhere by the end of 2029.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Within 14 days of entering the service, a young person would then meet with a named adviser.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Within four weeks, they would have their "personalised participation plan", setting out what both the support services and the young person involved would do, and when.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Jobs wise, Milburn wants there to be initiatives like work placements of up to 12 weeks, structured volunteering opportunities, and help to create businesses.

sentences.text: Sweeping reforms are needed to help 440,000 more young people into work, according to former minister Alan Milburn.

sentences.text: Almost one million young people aged 16 to 24 in the UK are not in education, employment or training - or "Neet" - a current rate of 13%, which Milburn wants to fall to around 5% within a decade.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: His government-commissioned review, due to be published in full on Tuesday, calls for ministers to intervene from early childhood through to adulthood, funded in part by radical changes to benefits for young adults.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: But Helen Whately, Conservative shadow work and pensions secretary, said Milburn's proposals were in parts "too cautious" and too reliant on the "expensive hand of the state".

sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: "We've got to get on with it, it's going to take time but I want to make sure every young person has a chance to earn or learn," he told BBC Breakfast on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: The review says that, in 2024/25, for every £1 spent helping young people into work or education, £25 was spent on youth benefits.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review
